topic: Agent Skills Marketplace Guide 2026: Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI

competitors.title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
key_points: Anthropic frames Agent Skills as organized folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude can discover and load dynamically for specific tasks
Skills are positioned as a composable way to package procedural knowledge instead of building one-off custom agents
The skill format centers on a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter metadata, plus optional supporting files for deeper context
Anthropic emphasizes progressive disclosure: load only the name and description first, then pull the full skill only when relevant
Skills can include executable code, which gives Claude deterministic tools for tasks better handled outside token generation
Anthropic says Skills are supported across Claude.ai, Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK, and the Claude Developer Platform

competitors.title: Agent Skills - Codex | OpenAI Developers
key_points: OpenAI positions skills as task-specific capabilities that extend Codex with instructions, resources, and optional scripts
Codex uses progressive disclosure, starting with each skill's name, description, and file path before loading full SKILL.md content
Skills can be invoked explicitly or selected implicitly when the task matches the skill description
The docs define the skill structure as a directory with SKILL.md plus optional scripts, references, assets, and agent metadata
OpenAI supports curated skill installation through the skill installer and also allows repository-scoped skills for teams
The product message is about making Codex more reliable for repeatable workflows, not just code generation

competitors.title: Extend Cursor with plugins
key_points: Cursor's marketplace strategy is broader than skills alone: it bundles plugins, skills, rules, hooks, commands, and MCP servers
The launch post emphasizes a curated partner set spanning the product development lifecycle, from design to deployment and testing
Users can discover prebuilt plugins in the Cursor Marketplace or create and share their own with the community
Cursor positions plugins as a way to orchestrate the entire development workflow in one place, not just improve prompting
The marketplace is clearly designed around team adoption and ecosystem expansion rather than a single-agent workflow
Cursor's newer releases add team and workspace customization, which makes distribution and governance part of the product story

competitors.title: Level Up Your Agents: Announcing Google's Official Skills Repository
key_points: Google's skills story is centered on an official repository that can be installed with npx skills install github.com/google/skills
The announcement explicitly supports Antigravity, Gemini CLI, and third-party agents, signaling cross-tool portability
Google also frames skills as a way to add agent context and workflow guidance, similar to the broader open agent skills standard
The adjacent Gemini CLI extensions work adds structured settings, secure secret storage, and workspace-scoped configuration
Google's Skill Registry documentation describes a secure, private, low-latency repository for managing skills
For consumer positioning, Gemini CLI is being transitioned to Antigravity CLI, with Gemini CLI requests for consumer tiers stopping on June 18, 2026

stats.fact: Anthropic published Agent Skills as an open standard for cross-platform portability on December 18, 2025.
stats.source: Anthropic engineering post on Agent Skills

stats.fact: OpenAI's Codex skills docs say Codex loads only a skill's metadata first and reads the full SKILL.md only when it decides the skill is relevant.
Cursor now supports Agent Skills in both the editor and CLI, and its Marketplace adds plugins, MCP servers, and team/workspace management in one place.
Google's official skills repository is installable via npx and is meant to work across Antigravity, Gemini CLI, and other third-party agents.
stats.source: Google Cloud blog on official skills repository

stats.fact: Google's Skill Registry is described as secure, private, and low-latency, which makes it a stronger enterprise distribution story than a public marketplace.
Consumer Gemini CLI access is in transition to Antigravity CLI, with consumer requests stopping on June 18, 2026.
